reason: Checked against the project's rules. stop_y (&C6) is read only by the CPY at line 1823 (grep across src and tools). The only ways into part_byte are the two BCS last_cell branches, at 1766 and 1805, and both pass through DEC A / STA, so the immediate operand is always written before it is compared. The second .part_byte at line 2145 is a different scope and never uses stop_y. draw_column lives in bank 4 sideways RAM and already modifies its own mask_operand_2 and pix_operand_2 in the same paged state, and no interrupt runs it. Dropping the write to &C6: restore_game_zp does not restore &C6 (render_zp.6502), so the logic already writes it before reading it after a render (game.6502:2763 says frames is no longer written; mover_x_max_high, result_high and y are all written first in game and scroll_hazel). The front-end users of &C6 (title_offset, bank5's result_high, zxwrk) run when the renderer does not. Every PROTECTED line, generated source, table and piece of raster-timed code is left alone. Room: bank 4 grows by 1 byte. Its end is &B37D in the shipping build (131 bytes free under REN_BASE) and &B3F6 in the gameplay build (10 free), so it fits. Cycles: each loop iteration saves 1 (CPY zp 3 -> CPY # 2, 94.9/3 = 31.6 a pass) and each entry costs 1 (STA zp 3 -> STA abs 4, 28.2/3 = 9.4 a pass), net about 22.2 a pass, about 0.7 for each loop compare. Bytes: +1 (the claim's -1 saved).
